considerations: Check for shared VPNs, mobile roaming and normal tool use.
Review sign-in and token activity before deciding whether it is suspicious.
description: Look for successful device-code sign-ins from multiple addresses for one user and app in fifteen minutes.

evidence.claim: Microsoft demonstrated in a lab that device code phishing can expose sessions used by coding agents, and noted earlier device-code phishing campaigns. The demonstration is distinct from observed incidents.

expected_output: One row per user, app and fifteen-minute window.

history.summary: Created evidence-backed hunt and validated all supported variants.

hypothesis: Look for successful device-code sign-ins from multiple addresses for one user and app in fifteen minutes.
performance: Time filter first, then table-specific predicates and a narrow projection.
scope: Evidence review, static checks, Microsoft Kusto syntax and schema analysis. Engine and workspace execution not run.
title: Device-Code Grants From Multiple Network Origins

1.json:
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where AuthenticationProtocol =~ "deviceCode" and ResultType == "0" and isnotempty(UserPrincipalName) and isnotempty(IPAddress)
| summarize SignIns = count(), Origins = dcount(IPAddress), Locations = make_set(Location, 8), Addresses = make_set(IPAddress, 12) by UserPrincipalName, AppDisplayName, Window = bin(TimeGenerated, 15m)
| where Origins >= 3
| order by Origins desc
| summarize Results = make_list(pack_all())
| project JSON = tostring(Results)
